reason: 2.1.1 draws the modal overlay on the full-viewport dialog itself and leaves ::backdrop to the browser, whose default dialog::backdrop background is rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1). A dialog opened with showModal() therefore had that 10% black layer under the overlay: it looked darker than the same dialog with the open attribute (light #e7e8eb in Chrome and #e8e9ec in Firefox, against #eeeff2), it left a grey #e5e5e5 page when --femto-modal-overlay-background-color was transparent, and it appeared before the overlay faded in and stayed until it had faded out, since the opening and closing animations run only on the dialog. femto sets :where(dialog)::backdrop to background: none, so a modal dialog renders like an open one and the overlay token alone sets the color. :where() keeps the rule at (0,0,1), so an author's own ::backdrop rule loaded after femto still overrides it, as it overrode the browser default in 2.1.1.
notes: Fixture: the three dialogs of components-modal-show.html (light island, dark island, plain), which page.js opens with showModal(). Probed with standalone Selenium pages in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160 beta, light and dark, ltr and rtl, at 500 and 1280px, with motion and reduced motion, with the token transparent, and with the opening animation frozen at 0s and 0.4s: every corner pixel of a showModal() dialog now matches the open-attribute dialog (light #eeeff2, dark #0b0c0f in Chrome and #0a0c0e in Firefox, token transparent #ffffff and #13171f, t=0 #ffffff), and open-attribute dialogs keep their 2.1.1 pixels. With focus inside the dialog, whole screenshots of the two are identical; on a dialog with nothing focusable Chrome also draws its focus ring at the viewport edge, with 2.1.1 as with femto. Author rules after femto still win: ::backdrop { background: rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5) } and dialog::backdrop { ... } keep their 2.1.1 pixels, an author ::backdrop background-image now shows without the browser tint under it, and a [popover]::backdrop rule is unaffected. Safari was not probed (safaridriver could not start a session); WebKit's UA stylesheet has the same dialog::backdrop { background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) } rule. Upstream issue picocss/pico#565.

reason: Computed style only, from modal-dialog-backdrop-tint. Firefox and Safari apply their default dialog::backdrop background, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1), to every dialog and report it for closed and open-attribute dialogs too, but only a modal dialog draws a backdrop. femto's :where(dialog)::backdrop { background: none } clears it on every dialog, so these dialogs compute rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) and render exactly as in 2.1.1.
notes: Seen in Firefox 160 beta on the closed, open and shadow-root dialogs of components-modal.html, classes-modal.html, kitchen-sink.html, tokens-base.html, tokens-schemes.html, tokens-breakpoints.html and utilities-reduce-motion.html; Chrome 158 reports rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) for those dialogs with 2.1.1 and femto alike. Safari is listed because WebKit's UA stylesheet uses the same unconditional dialog::backdrop rule as Firefox and the harness reads ::backdrop on a closed dialog in all three browsers; it was not run. Open-attribute screenshots are unchanged in Chrome and Firefox. Upstream issue picocss/pico#565.

reason: 2.1.1 spaces the buttons of a modal footer with margin-left on each one after the first. In right-to-left text the buttons run from right to left, so the gap fell after each button instead of before it, and the first two buttons had none between them. femto uses margin-inline-start, so the gap falls between the buttons in either direction, and in left-to-right text it computes as before. A [role=group] in the footer needs it too: its overlap margin is now margin-inline-start (group-rtl-logical-corners), which replaces the footer gap, where the footer's margin-left would have opened a gap of half the spacing between its items in right-to-left text.
notes: Fixture: the footers of components-modal.html, components-modal-show.html and classes-modal.html, whose buttons and role=button links run in the rtl legs of those pages. Probed with a standalone Selenium page in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160 beta at 390 and 1280px: an open dialog whose footer holds a three-button [role=group], two buttons and a role=button link. In right-to-left text the gap between the two plain buttons moved to their seam (gaps from left to right went from [10, 0] to [0, 10] at 1280, the mirror of left-to-right's [10, 0]), and the footer group went from seams of 1.25 and 0px with a 1.25px overhang (2.1.1 and femto before) to 1.25 and 1.25px with none. With the group fix but the footer still on margin-left, each group item after the first had margins 10px / -1.25px and the seam between the second and third opened 8.75px (7px at 390). Left-to-right footers are unchanged.

reason: 2.1.1 floats the close control of a modal header right, with its spacing on its left. In right-to-left text that is the start side, so the control sat against the first letter of the title and the other end of the header stayed empty. femto floats it to the inline end, with margin-inline-start (modal-close-inline-end-rtl), so in right-to-left text it sits at the top left, the mirror of left-to-right text. Left-to-right text looks the same, but getComputedStyle reports float as inline-end instead of right.
notes: Fixture: the header close controls of components-modal.html, components-modal-show.html and classes-modal.html (button[rel=prev], a[rel=prev], a.close and button.close), in ltr and in the rtl legs those pages run, and of the closed dialogs in kitchen-sink.html. Probed with a standalone Selenium page in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160 beta at 390, 700 and 1280px, light and dark, with dir=rtl on <html> and on the dialog itself: in rtl, 2.1.1 leaves the close control flush right, 20px from the start of the title at 1280 and 16px at 390, where ltr leaves 319.47px in Chrome and 320.17px in Firefox at 1280; femto puts it flush left with the ltr gap to the title at every width. A dir=ltr dialog in an rtl page, and every ltr box, hover and focus state, measure as with 2.1.1. Upstream issue picocss/pico#661.

reason: In right-to-left text 2.1.1 keeps a modal close control's spacing on its left: margin-left in the header, and margin-left: auto outside it, which pushes the control to the right, the start side. femto uses margin-inline-start for both, so in right-to-left text the spacing sits on the control's right, the header control keeps its gap from the title, and a close control outside the header moves to the left, mirroring left-to-right text, where the margins compute as before.
notes: Fixture: the close controls of components-modal.html (with the closed one in a shadow root, whose auto margin computes as auto), components-modal-show.html and classes-modal.html (with the body button.close and span.close), and of the closed dialogs in kitchen-sink.html, in rtl legs. Probed with a standalone Selenium page in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160 beta at 390, 700 and 1280px: in rtl the header control's margins went from 20px left / 0 right to 0 / 20px at 1280 (16px at 390), and a close control outside the header from the right edge to the left edge, each the mirror of its ltr box. Upstream issue picocss/pico#661.

selector: dialog > article > footer, dialog > article > footer *
reason: 2.1.1 aligns a modal footer right. In right-to-left text that is the start side, so the buttons stayed at the bottom right while the rest of the modal ran the other way. femto aligns the footer to the inline end, so in right-to-left text the buttons line up at the bottom left, mirroring left-to-right text, under the close control's new top-left place (modal-close-float-inline-end). It also keeps every wrapped line flush with the edge: the gap now sits at each button's inline start (modal-footer-button-gap-rtl), which with right alignment would leave a right-to-left line that begins with a later button half a spacing in from the right edge. Left-to-right text looks the same, but the footer and the descendants that inherit its alignment report end instead of right.
notes: Fixture: the footers of components-modal.html, components-modal-show.html and classes-modal.html, in ltr and rtl; buttons and role=button links keep text-align: center. Probed with standalone Selenium pages in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160 beta at 390, 700 and 1280px: in rtl a three-button footer went from flush right to flush left, with offsets that mirror ltr (Chrome at 1280: 338px from the left and 0 from the right with 2.1.1, 0 and 328px with femto, against 328 and 0 in ltr). With right alignment and the inline-start gap, the wrapped 'Link button two' line of the components-modal.html footer sat 8.5px in from the right edge at 700px, and the second line of a five-button footer 8px at 390 and 8.5px at 700; with end alignment every line is flush. Every ltr line keeps its 2.1.1 position. Upstream issue picocss/pico#661.

reason: 2.1.1 caps the modal card at calc(100vh - spacing * 2). Mobile browsers with a retractable toolbar (Safari on iOS, Chrome on Android, Samsung Internet) size 100vh as if the toolbar were hidden, while the fixed, flex-centered dialog fills only the visible viewport. So while the toolbar showed, a tall card was taller than the dialog and centering pushed it past both edges: its header and close button were cut off at the top, and with the open attribute its footer buttons went under the toolbar, beyond the reach of the card's own scrolling (a dialog opened with showModal() scrolls down to the footer, but not up to the header). femto uses 100svh, the viewport height with the toolbar shown, so the card fits while the toolbar shows. While the toolbar is hidden, a tall card is up to the toolbar's height shorter than in 2.1.1, which fit it exactly, and stays centered with the extra space above and below; short modals are unaffected. Desktop browsers and iframes have no dynamic toolbar and 100svh equals 100vh there, so nothing changes.
notes: Documentation only, scoped to a mobile-dynamic-toolbar preset that does not exist: the harness iframes have no dynamic toolbar, so 100svh equals 100vh, the card's computed max-height is the same on both sides, and the "*" values never waive a real max-height difference on the modal fixtures (the open dialogs of components-modal.html, components-modal-show.html, classes-modal.html and tokens-breakpoints.html, and the closed ones of kitchen-sink.html, tokens-base.html, tokens-schemes.html and utilities-reduce-motion.html). Probed with a standalone Selenium page, a tall dialog whose card holds a header with a close button, 30 paragraphs and a footer with two buttons, at a 664px visible viewport with an 80px toolbar emulated: CDP Emulation.setSmallViewportHeightDifferenceOverride in Chrome 158, and windowUtils.setDynamicToolbarMaxHeight with dom.meta-viewport.enabled in Firefox 160 beta. In both browsers the 2.1.1 card spans -24 to 688px at 500px wide, with the close button's top at -13.5, and -22 to 686px at 1000px, with it at -10.1; femto's spans 16 to 648 and 18 to 646, with the close and footer buttons in view, for open-attribute and showModal() dialogs, ltr and rtl, light and dark. Without the toolbar, the 100svh build matches the 100vh build in every measurement and screenshot pixel in Chrome, Firefox and Safari 27.2. Upstream issue picocss/pico#514.

reason: 2.1.1 leaves a modal's scrolling free to chain to the page. On a page that does not add the modal-is-open class, which locks the page's scrolling, scrolling a modal card past its end scrolled the page behind the modal, and so did scrolling over the overlay of a dialog opened with showModal(). femto sets overscroll-behavior: contain on dialog and on dialog > article, so a card that has reached its end no longer scrolls the page. Browsers that also contain a scroll container with nothing to scroll (Chrome 144 and later, Firefox 150 and later) stop there as well when the pointer is over a short card or over the overlay of a dialog opened with showModal(). A dialog opened with the open attribute keeps the browser's overflow: visible, so it is not a scroll container: scrolling over its overlay still scrolls the page, as in 2.1.1. Pages that set modal-is-open behave as before.
notes: Seen on every dialog and dialog > article of classes-modal.html, components-modal.html (including the dialog in a shadow root), components-modal-show.html, kitchen-sink.html, tokens-base.html, tokens-breakpoints.html, tokens-schemes.html and utilities-reduce-motion.html, closed or open, in Chrome 158 and Firefox 161, every preset, leg, width, direction and state. Probed with a standalone Selenium page in Chrome 157: a 6000px page scrolled to 1000px, a dialog without modal-is-open whose card is scrolled to its end, and four 300px wheel steps. Over a long card at its end, 2.1.1 scrolls the page to 2200px and femto leaves it at 1000px, for showModal() and open-attribute dialogs, and the same over a short card with nothing to scroll. Over the overlay of a showModal() dialog, 2.1.1 scrolls the page to 3400px and femto leaves it at 1000px; over an open-attribute dialog's overlay both scroll it. Firefox 161 was not observed scrolling: in headless Firefox, WebDriver wheel and keyboard input ignore overscroll-behavior even on a plain scrollable div with contain, so only its computed values are confirmed. Safari was not run.
